title: Israeli slang
topic: informal expressions: סַבָּבָה, יַאלְלָה, אַחְלָה, בְּסֵדֶר
why: The spoken expressions you hear everywhere in Israel (sababa, yalla, akhla, takhles…), with their register so you know when to use them. The first lesson of the last unit: you move from textbook Hebrew to street Hebrew.

{"lessons": ["

Talking like an Israeli

Spoken Hebrew is very relaxed: there's no formal \"you,\" you speak to everyone the same way, and a lot of informal expressions are also heard at the office or in a store. But in official writing (a letter to city hall, an email to a government office), people avoid them.

Several come from Arabic (יַאלְלָה, אַחְלָה, סַבָּבָּה, כֵּיף), others from Yiddish (תַּכְלֶס).

ExpressionMeaningRegister
בְּסֵדֶרokay, all right [be-seder]everyday, with everyone
אֵין בְּעָיָהno problem [ein be'aya]everyday
בְּכֵּיףmy pleasure [be-kef]everyday, warm
סַבָּבָּהokay, cool [sababa]informal
אַחְלָהgreat [akhla]informal
יַאלְלָהcome on!, let's go! [yalla]informal

The trap: בְּסֵדֶר and סַבָּבָּה both mean \"OK,\" but סַבָּבָּה is for friends or coworkers. With a stranger, at the bank or at the doctor's, בְּסֵדֶר is safer.

", "

Saying yes, saying it's awesome

To accept: סַבָּבָּה, בְּסֵדֶר, אֵין בְּעָיָה. To reply to a thank-you: בְּכֵּיף, \"my pleasure,\" which you hear on every street corner.

— תּוֹדָה עַל הָעֶזְרָה! — בְּכֵּיף!— Thanks for the help! — My pleasure! [toda al ha-ezra! — be-kef!]

אַחְלָה goes before the noun and doesn't agree, unlike adjectives: אַחְלָה יוֹם, אַחְלָה מְסִבָּה. מַגְנִיב, on the other hand, is a real adjective, placed after the noun and agreeing with it: סֶרֶט מַגְנִיב, מְסִבָּה מַגְנִיבָה.

הַהוֹפָעָה הָיְתָה חֲבָל עַל הַזְּמַן!The concert was awesome! [ha-hofa'a hayta khaval al ha-zman!]

Watch out: חֲבָל on its own means \"too bad.\" But חֲבָל עַל הַזְּמַן, literally \"a pity about the time,\" means \"awesome, amazing\" in slang. And in words borrowed from other languages, the dot (dagesh) keeps the b or k sound: סַבָּבָּה [sababa], בְּכֵּיף [be-kef].

", "

Checking in, hurrying, getting to the point

ExpressionMeaning
מָה נִשְׁמָע?what's new?, how are you? (lit. \"what is heard?\") [ma nishma?]
מָה קוֹרֶה?what's up?, what's going on? [ma kore?]
נוּwell?, come on! (impatience) [nu]
תַּכְלֶסbottom line, for real [takhles]
כְּאִלּוּlike, as if [ke'ilu]
אֵין מַצָּבno way!, no chance! [ein matsav]
יֵשׁ מַצָּבcould be, maybe [yesh matsav]
סְתָםfor no reason, just because; just kidding! [stam]
נוּ, יַאלְלָה, אֲנַחְנוּ מְאַחֲרִים!Come on, hurry up, we're late! [nu, yalla, anakhnu me'akharim!]
תַּכְלֶס, מָה עוֹשִׂים הָעֶרֶב?Bottom line, what are we doing tonight? [takhles, ma osim ha-erev?]

כְּאִלּוּ is used as a filler word, exactly like \"like\" among young English speakers: good to understand, use in moderation.

You reply to מָה נִשְׁמָע? with הַכֹּל בְּסֵדֶר or אַחְלָה, not with a long story: like \"how's it going?\" in English, it's mostly a greeting.
